 Dated this the 4th day of September 2025
Petitioner/s: Sri. Nagaraju H.S
 S/o Siddashetty,
 Aged about 58 years,
 R/at No.68/1, 17th A main,
 4th Block, Nandini Layout,
 Bengaluru North,
 Bengaluru - 560 096.
 (By Sri. Ramakrishnaiah K, Adv.)

 W/o Ravindra,
 No.27, 1st A Cross, Goraguntepalya,
 Yeshwanthpura, Bengaluru - 560 022.

 :Judgment:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Nagaraju in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 03.09.2018.

Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
1 2.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 03.09.2018 at about 8.10 a.m., when the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HF- 2091 slowly, carefully and cautiously observing all traffic rules and regulations, proceeding on the left side of M.E.I road and when he reached near Lakshmidevi hotel, Smashana road, Yeshwanthpura lorry stand, Bengaluru, at that time, respondent's Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-C-2955 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle,
due to which, petitioner was thrown out from his motorcycle and sustained severe injuries.

3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to People Tree Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of the notice issued to the Respondent she appeared through her Counsel and filed Objection to the claim petition.

The Respondent has filed written statement submitting as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent that the petitioner himself was tortfeasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.
The petitioner himself fell down from the motorcycle and false complaint was lodged SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 against this respondent's vehicle.
It is submitted that the petitioner was not having valid driving license at time of the accident.

It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary,
unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 20.06.2022 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 03.09.2018 at about 8.10 a.m., near Lakshmi Devi Hotel, Smashana Road, Yeshwanthapura Lorry Stand, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Regn.
KA-05-C-2955 ?
SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
2 2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

3) What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 15 and the Respondent has examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 8.
7. Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8.
Issue No.1
: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-C-2955.
9.

On this point the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 03.09.2018 at about 8.10 a.m. he being the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HF-2091 was riding slowly and carefully and proceeding on the left side of MEI road and when he reached near Lakshmidevi hotel, Smashana road, Yeshwanthapura lorry stand,
Bengaluru and at the time the driver of the offending vehicle came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle
, as a result, petitioner was thrown out from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which discloses that the case has SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and sec.134(a&b) of IMV Act.
In addition Ex.P3 - Spot mahazar and sketch which discloses that the accident has taken place at distance of 10 feet from south towards north.

The spot mahazar discloses that offending vehicle was proceeding from MEI main road towards outer ring road and the petitioner was coming from the opposite direction and the offending vehicle dashed the motorcycle of the petitioner resulting in the accident.

In addition Ex.P7 - IMV report discloses that the front portion of the front bumper of the offending vehicle has been damaged and the front side of the motorcycle also damaged which goes to show that it is head on collision.

On perusal of the said documents it discloses that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
3 offending vehicle.
11.
As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by learned counsel for Respondent SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019
and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he stated that there is no signal and stated that the accident has taken place due to the fault of the offending vehicle.
It is denied that the road was narrow road and denied that he was entering from Kanteerava Studio towards MEI road at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has admitted that road is a junction and he was taking right turn at the junction and stated that he was wearing helmet at the time of the accident.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioners side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also declined the SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P6 which discloses that the petitioner was admitted in People Tree hospital under the history of RTA and had sustained grievous injuries to his head and right leg multiple comminuted open fracture and Ex.P8 to 10 - Discharge summaries shows that the petitioner has taken treatment from 03.09.2018 to 04.10.2018, 19.10.2018 to 24.10.2018 and 19.12.2018 to 25.12.20218.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P11 - medical bills and it is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent that the bills at Sl.No.8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 28, 34, 35, 37 to 39, 49,
50, 53, 54 are xerox bills.

However on perusal of the bills produced by the petitioner it discloses that the amount paid by the sponsor Medi Assist India TPA Pvt. Ltd., had not been deducted in the list of calculation and hence an amount of Rs.2 lkhs paid by the sponser is deducted out of the total calculated amount.

entities.text: Medi Assist India TPA Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence except suggesting that the said bills are xerox bills nothing is elicited to prove that the said amount is already claimed by the SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 petitioner.

Hence, in view of the medical bills produced by the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
4 Rs.10,93,228/- minus Rs.2,00,000/- paid by the sponser which equals to Rs.8,93,228/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained severe head injury and right leg multiple comminuted open fracture both bones and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and he cannot stand or walk without support,
cannot walk fast, run, cannot squat, cannot sit with cross legs, cannot climb stairs or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:

In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 58 years and he was working as Clerk at The Mysore Electrical Industries Ltd., Bengaluru and drawing Rs.30,000/- p.m. PW.1 in his cross- examination has deposed he cannot examine the company official and cannot produce company documents to prove his employment in the said company.
16.

On the other hand the respondent has examined Deputy Manager HR of Mysore Electrical Industries as RW.1 and in his evidence he has deposed that petitioner is retired from service on 30.06.2020 and retiring benefits are granted and he had obtained 155 days medical leave and during that period he was paid salary and also given promotion and other allowances.
He was on leave from 03.09.2018 to 08.03.2019 and he continued his job from 08.03.2019.
In his cross- SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 examination RW.1 has deposed that he was working from 01.02.1981 to 30.06.2020 and he has benefit under medical leave fund.
RW.1 has also deposed that he had continued work after the accident and treatment.
In support of the same RW1 has also produced the ExR1 To ExR8.
Hence, these documents substantiate that the petitioner has not suffered any loss of income due to laid up period.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled any compensation amount under this head.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The Petitioner has not adduced any evidence to show he has sustained permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence in the absence of any evidence it has to be concluded that the petitioner has not sustained any permanent disability in the said accident.
18. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
5 SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 19. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant and it can be assumed that the petitioner has spent considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet and conveyance.

Hence,
the amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid Nil up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses 8,93,228/-
 Total 9,63,228/-

SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 9,63,228/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
21.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

entities.text:
SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Eicher canter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-C-2955.
It is admitted by both the petitioner and respondent that the offending vehicle was not insured as on the date of the accident.

In this case, SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019 the Respondent is the R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle Therefore, the Respondent has to pay the Nagaraju H.S vs Pushpavathi.H on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187741525/
6 compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 9,63,228/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner and directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
SCCH 15 MVC No.1508/2019
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

(RESHMA JANE RODRIGUES) XIII Addl.
Small Causes Judge, ACJM, Court of Small Causes & Member, MACT-15, Bengaluru.
